newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel warns Serbia over treatment of opposition.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel warns Serbia over treatment of opposition.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel warned Serbia on Wednesday its decision to annul local election victories by opposition parties and its crackdown on independent radio stations was unacceptable.
He said European Union foreign ministers, meeting in Brussels on Friday, would have to look seriously at whether they should offer any economic support to the Serbian government.
"What is going on in Belgrade at the moment is an attack on peoples' democratic rights," Kinkel told parliament in a statement on the role of human rights in foreign policy.
"Anyone who deprives citizens of their vote and their rights will have difficulty finding the path to Europe," he said.
"Annulling elections which have taken place democratically is not acceptable," Kinkel stressed.

The United Nations last year removed trade sanctions on Serbia. But an "outer wall" of sanctions remains, denying Serbia access to money from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, as well as membership in the United Nations and other organisations.
Karl-Heinz Hornhues, chairman of parliament's foreign affairs committee, said it would be wrong to loosen any of the remaining restrictions at the moment.
More than 120,000 opposition supporters flooded central Belgrade on Wednesday for a 17th day of demonstrations against Milosevic's ruling Socialist Party.
